name: Story-to-Insight
description: Personal story that ends with a transferable insight or lesson
example: Told a story about getting rejected from 12 companies before Amex, ending with 'rejection is just redirection'

name: Data-to-Opinion
description: Lead with a surprising stat then share your hot take on it
example: '73% of PMs have never spoken to a customer.' Then opinion on why discovery is broken.

name: Listicle
description: Numbered list of tips/tools/lessons with brief explanations
example: '7 tools that saved me 10 hours a week as a PM' with one-liner per tool

name: Before-After
description: Show transformation — what changed and how
example: Before: 60-hour weeks drowning in Jira. After: 30-hour weeks shipping 2x. Here's what changed.

name: Hot-Take
description: Bold contrarian opinion that challenges conventional wisdom
example: 'Product roadmaps are a lie we tell stakeholders to feel in control.'

name: How-To-Guide
description: Step-by-step actionable tutorial on a specific skill
example: How I run a stakeholder alignment meeting in 15 minutes flat. Step 1...

name: Myth-Busting
description: Take a common belief and systematically dismantle it
example: 'You need an MBA to break into product management.' No you don't. Here's why.

name: Day-in-Life
description: Walk through a typical day with behind-the-scenes details
example: 5:30 AM alarm. 6 AM gym. 7:30 AM standup prep. Here's what a PM's day actually looks like at Amex.

name: Lessons-Learned
description: Distilled lessons from a specific experience or time period
example: 3 years at Amex taught me more about people than about products. Here are 5 lessons.

name: Framework-Share
description: Share a mental model or decision framework you use
example: My 2x2 matrix for deciding what to build next. Effort vs Impact is lazy. Try this instead.

name: Comparison
description: Compare two approaches/tools/mindsets side by side
example: Product Manager vs Project Manager. Same meeting. Completely different questions.

name: Unpopular-Opinion
description: State an opinion most people disagree with and defend it
example: Unpopular opinion: standups are just status meetings wearing agile costumes.

name: Failure-Story
description: Share a professional failure and what you learned from it
example: I once shipped a feature nobody asked for. Took 3 sprints. Got zero adoption. Here's what went wrong.

name: Behind-the-Scenes
description: Reveal what actually happens behind a process or decision
example: What actually happens in an Amex product review. Spoiler: it's not what the Agile textbook says.

name: Challenge-Post
description: Challenge your audience to do something for a set period
example: Challenge: talk to 3 customers this week. No survey. No form. Just a conversation.

name: Case-Study
description: Break down a real product/business decision with analysis
example: How Zomato's 10-minute delivery bet changed the entire food-tech game in India.

name: Book-Summary
description: Key takeaways from a book applied to your domain
example: Read 'Inspired' by Marty Cagan. 3 things that changed how I write PRDs.

name: Tool-Review
description: Honest review of a tool you actually use with pros and cons
example: I replaced Notion with Obsidian for PM documentation. Here's my honest take after 6 months.

name: Career-Advice
description: Direct advice on navigating career decisions
example: You don't need to 'find your passion.' You need to find what you're willing to be bored doing on a Tuesday.

name: Interview-Tips
description: Tactical advice for cracking interviews in your domain
example: The PM interview question that trips up 90% of candidates. And how to nail it.

name: Observation-Post
description: Share something you noticed and unpack why it matters
example: I noticed the best PMs in my org never say 'I think.' They say 'the data suggests.' Small shift. Big difference.

name: Thread-Style
description: Multi-part post that builds on itself like a Twitter thread
example: 1/ The startup advice nobody gives you. 2/ Your first hire matters more than your first feature. 3/...

name: Analogy-Post
description: Explain a complex concept through a relatable analogy
example: Product management is like being a GPS. You don't drive. You recalculate.

name: Confession-Post
description: Admit something vulnerable that others relate to
example: Confession: I still get nervous before every stakeholder presentation. 3 years in.

name: Prediction-Post
description: Make a bold prediction about your industry's future
example: By 2027 half of all PM tasks will be automated by AI. Here's what that means for your career.

name: Rant-Post
description: Controlled rant about something broken in your industry
example: Can we please stop asking PMs to 'just quickly build a dashboard'? That's not how any of this works.

name: Gratitude-Post
description: Thank someone or something that shaped your journey
example: My manager at Amex told me something in week 1 that I still think about every day.

name: Milestone-Post
description: Celebrate a professional milestone with reflection
example: 1000 days at Amex today. Here's what I wish I knew on day 1.

name: Question-Post
description: Pose a genuine question to spark discussion
example: If you could only measure ONE metric for your product what would it be? And why?

name: Contrarian-How-To
description: Teach something by doing the opposite of conventional advice
example: How to fail your next product launch in 5 easy steps. (Do the opposite.)

name: Letter-Format
description: Write a letter to your past/future self or someone else
example: Dear 22-year-old me sitting in IIT Delhi. You're about to make the scariest decision of your life.

name: Mini-Poll
description: Present 2-3 options and ask audience to vote in comments
example: Which skill matters more for a PM in 2026? A) SQL B) Storytelling C) AI prompting. Drop your answer below.

name: One-Liner-Expansion
description: Start with a punchy one-liner then expand on it in the body
example: 'Strategy is just saying no with a spreadsheet.' Let me explain.

name: Curated-List
description: Curated collection of resources/people/tools on a theme
example: 5 newsletters every Indian PM should subscribe to. None of them are obvious.

name: Reaction-Post
description: React to a trending news/event with your professional lens
example: Byju's just laid off another 1000 people. Here's what edtech founders aren't talking about.
